items.title: Semiconductor stocks suffered a broad selloff as investors reassessed the AI trade following Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO, r
items.content_excerpt: Semiconductor stocks suffered a broad selloff as investors reassessed the AI trade following Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO, raising concerns about the company's leadership, competitive position and its central role in financing and supplying the AI ecosystem. AMD plunged 8.75%, while the PHLX Semiconductor Index fell 3.43%, reversing part of its earlier gains. Other major decliners included SanDisk (-5.59%), Broadcom (-4.76%), Dell Technologies (-7.18%), CoreWeave (-6.13%), Micron (-2.52%) and Intel (-2.52%). Nvidia also dropped 2.01%, while the S&P 500 declined 0.40%. Initially, investors expected Nvidia's weakening position to benefit competitors through increased market share, stronger pricing power and new opportunities for alternative chip suppliers. However, uncertainty surrounding Huang's departure and the company's ongoing investigation into potential exposure of business secrets has shifted sentiment across the sector. $AMD $NVDA $AVGO $SNDK

items.title: Marsh Re expects the recent Microsoft 365 and Exchange Online outage to have a minimal impact on the insurance market, as the uneven nature
items.content_excerpt: Marsh Re expects the recent Microsoft 365 and Exchange Online outage to have a minimal impact on the insurance market, as the uneven nature of the disruption and limited financial losses are unlikely to generate significant insurance claims. Most affected companies are expected to face short-term productivity losses and operational delays rather than substantial business interruptions. The reinsurance broker noted that cyber insurance policies generally cover contingent business interruptions caused by third-party service provider failures, whether accidental or malicious. However, coverage depends on policy waiting periods, which average around four hours for smaller organizations and 12 hours or more for larger companies. To qualify for coverage, affected businesses must experience disruptions exceeding their applicable waiting periods and demonstrate actual lost profits. $MSFT

items.content_excerpt: Google and Samsung have opened preorders for nine new AI-powered smart-glasses models developed with Warby Parker and Gentle Monster, challenging Meta’s leadership in the market. Six Gentle Monster models will cost $449, while three Warby Parker versions will start at $395. Deliveries are scheduled to begin December 10. Powered by Google’s Gemini assistant and Android XR, the glasses feature a 12-megapixel camera, voice controls, real-time translation, navigation, calls, messaging and music playback. They weigh approximately 41 grams, offer up to nine hours of battery life and are compatible with iPhones and selected Android devices. Privacy is a key focus: recording indicators prevent capture if covered or tampered with, while Google says faces of bystanders are blurred before visual information is processed by Gemini. Users must also agree not to record people without consent or film in sensitive locations. $GOOGL $SSNLF $META

items.title: Semiconductor stocks suffered a broad selloff as investors reassessed the AI trade following Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO, r
items.content_excerpt: Semiconductor stocks suffered a broad selloff as investors reassessed the AI trade following Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO, raising concerns about the company's leadership, competitive position and its central role in financing and supplying the AI ecosystem. AMD plunged 8.75%, while the PHLX Semiconductor Index fell 3.43%, reversing part of its earlier gains. Other major decliners included SanDisk (-5.59%), Broadcom (-4.76%), Dell Technologies (-7.18%), CoreWeave (-6.13%), Micron (-2.52%) and Intel (-2.52%). Nvidia also dropped 2.01%, while the S&P 500 declined 0.40%. Initially, investors expected Nvidia's weakening position to benefit competitors through increased market share, stronger pricing power and new opportunities for alternative chip suppliers. However, uncertainty surrounding Huang's departure and the company's ongoing investigation into potential exposure of business secrets has shifted sentiment across the sector. $AMD $NVDA $AVGO $SNDK

items.content_excerpt: $NU The real reason the street hates this stock is because it proves with math that 'poor people' are better banking customers than 'rich people' at scale. Its better to have 1 million poor people with 1 dollar loans than a million dollar loan to 1 rich person. Why? It makes more money. But what about the extra risk of extra loans? You see it in the NPL's. But I say this take Bolsonaro for example -- if Donald Trump defaults on his debts to you? You lose everything. Flee to Miami. What happens if a "peasant" defaults on their debts to you? You lose a pack of cigarettes. A small fixed cost imbedded within another loan repayment structure whos intense interest costs they're grateful to repay, because no where else they have access to expanding pools of capital that creates the potential for social stratification.

items.title: $DRTS Alpha Tau’s REGAIN trial (recurrent GBM) presented at SNO 2026: 6 evaluable patients, 100% ORR, 83.3% CR. All 8 treated patients alive
items.content_excerpt: $DRTS Alpha Tau’s REGAIN trial (recurrent GBM) presented at SNO 2026: 6 evaluable patients, 100% ORR, 83.3% CR. All 8 treated patients alive at median 6.9 months follow-up — median OS not yet reached. What stands out: the first 3 patients showed 2/3 CR. The next 3 patients: 3/3 CR. The response rate is improving as enrollment expands, not regressing toward the mean. Zero unanticipated serious adverse events. 100% technical feasibility. For a disease where median OS is ~6-9 months with current standard of care, these are remarkable early signals. Investor call Monday 8:30 ET.

items.title: $AG $B Could Barrick's North American Gold IPO Set the Stage for a Jerritt Canyon Acquisition? The timing is certainly intriguing. Barri
items.content_excerpt: $AG $B Could Barrick's North American Gold IPO Set the Stage for a Jerritt Canyon Acquisition? The timing is certainly intriguing. Barrick just announced plans to IPO its North American gold assets in early 2027, potentially creating a well-capitalized platform for further consolidation in Nevada. Meanwhile, First Majestic is aggressively advancing Jerritt Canyon, investing approximately $42M in Q3 alone. During AG's recent earnings call, Keith Neumeyer expressed considerable excitement about upcoming exploration results, saying management was anxious to release some very interesting discoveries. Now consider the strategic fit: - Jerritt Canyon sits north and northeast of Nevada's prolific Carlin Trend, home to major Barrick and Newmont operations. - The property contains substantial gold resources, established infrastructure, and a long history of production. - AG anticipates releasing updated resource figures in early 2027, around the same time as Barrick's planned IPO. - Mining is targeted to restart in Q3 2027, with initial gold production in Q4. - Consolidation could create economies of scale in exploration, procurement, engineering, and operations. - A newly public American Barrick could potentially have greater flexibility to fund acquisitions through cash, debt, or equity. Here's what makes this particularly interesting: First Majestic is investing heavily to advance and potentially de-risk Jerritt Canyon just as Barrick is preparing to establish a separately traded North American gold powerhouse. A compelling exploration update could meaningfully increase Jerritt Canyon's strategic value before either company's major 2027 milestones. For First Majestic, an attractive acquisition offer could unlock substantial value while allowing management to concentrate capital on its core silver operations. To be clear, there is no confirmed acquisition discussion. This is a potential strategic opportunity, not an announced transaction. But with gold possibly bottoming here and back above $4,000 into strong seasonality, Barrick preparing its IPO, and First Majestic promising interesting exploration results... Jerritt Canyon deserves considerably more attention imo.

items.content_excerpt: Barrick Mining has filed an SEC registration for an IPO to spin off its core North American gold assets into American Barrick Gold Corp., which plans to list on the NYSE under ABGC while remaining a controlled subsidiary. items.content_excerpt: $AAL $DAL $UAL $JETS The FAA's nationwide ground stop is lifted, and the verified story is less dramatic than the stream. Cause, per the FAA: a communications issue hitting the Air Route Traffic Control Centers. Transportation Sec. Duffy blamed "an incredibly old air traffic control system." Verified: • No sign of a cyber attack so far, per DHS Sec. Mullin. Root cause still under investigation. • Eurocontrol paused US-bound departures from its 42 member states at the FAA's request. • About 1.5M travelers stranded (Cirium estimate). Cancellations run into the weekend. What I'm not buying from the feed: "an AI agent escaped," "it's Azure," "coordinated cyber attack." None of it is backed by the FAA or DHS. For the airlines, a one-off ATC outage is a bad weekend, not a thesis change. Not financial advice.

items.title: The FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop affecting all U.S. airports on Friday afternoon after extraordinary safety concerns arose from air
items.content_excerpt: The FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop affecting all U.S. airports on Friday afternoon after extraordinary safety concerns arose from air traffic control communication failures across all Air Route Traffic Control Centers. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy confirmed the nationwide disruption, requiring all departing flights to remain grounded until further notice, while incoming international flights were handled on a case-by-case basis. The disruption pressured airline stocks across the sector, including Southwest, American Airlines, Delta, United Airlines and JetBlue. Southwest had declared its 191st consecutive quarterly dividend of $0.18 per share a day earlier, but the routine capital return offered little support amid operational concerns. The broader market also weakened, with the S&P 500 falling 0.3%, the Dow Jones declining 0.2% and the Nasdaq losing 0.4%, amid pressure from semiconductor stocks. $LUV $AAL $DAL $UAL

items.title: PepsiCo plans to eliminate approximately 1,000 jobs across North America over the coming week as part of a broader restructuring aimed at st
items.content_excerpt: PepsiCo plans to eliminate approximately 1,000 jobs across North America over the coming week as part of a broader restructuring aimed at streamlining operations, improving efficiency and reversing sluggish sales in its domestic market. The company employs around 306,000 people worldwide, including approximately 125,000 in the U.S. The layoffs follow disappointing third-quarter performance, with North American beverage volumes declining 2% and food volumes remaining flat. In October, PepsiCo lowered its full-year 2026 earnings outlook, citing persistent weakness in its core market. Despite price cuts and increased marketing investments, management acknowledged that the turnaround is taking longer than expected. PepsiCo aims to simplify its organizational structure while continuing to invest in its brands and growth initiatives. Shares were slightly higher Monday but remain down nearly 1% year to date, underperforming the S&P 500, which has gained approximately 11%. $PEP

Semiconductor stocks suffered a broad selloff as investors reassessed the AI trade following Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO, raising concerns about the company's leadership, competitive position and its central role in financing and supplying the AI ecosystem. AMD plunged 8.75%, while the PHLX Semiconductor Index fell 3.43%, reversing part of its earlier gains. Other major decliners included SanDisk (-5.59%), Broadcom (-4.76%), Dell Technologies (-7.18%), CoreWeave (-6.13%), Micron (-2.52%) and Intel (-2.52%). Nvidia also dropped 2.01%, while the S&P 500 declined 0.40%. Initially, investors expected Nvidia's weakening position to benefit competitors through increased market share, stronger pricing power and new opportunities for alternative chip suppliers. However, uncertainty surrounding Huang's departure and the company's ongoing investigation into potential exposure of business secrets has shifted sentiment across the sector. $AMD $NVDA $AVGO $SNDK

messages.body: @Dutchholdem 5 complete responses out of 6 evaluable in recurrent GBM is not a normal early print imo. $DRTS trial only goes to 20 patients too, so Monday 8:30 ET call matters for how fast the rest enroll and how long those responses are holding

$DRTS Alpha Tau’s REGAIN trial (recurrent GBM) presented at SNO 2026: 6 evaluable patients, 100% ORR, 83.3% CR. All 8 treated patients alive at median 6.9 months follow-up — median OS not yet reached. What stands out: the first 3 patients showed 2/3 CR. The next 3 patients: 3/3 CR. The response rate is improving as enrollment expands, not regressing toward the mean. Zero unanticipated serious adverse events. 100% technical feasibility. For a disease where median OS is ~6-9 months with current standard of care, these are remarkable early signals. Investor call Monday 8:30 ET.

$DRTS I simply go by what the FDA authorized just a month ago which was to dramatically approve the expansion of scope and size of the trial very likely with continuing real time feedback and discussion with Alpha Tau and most likely the core of the data we will soon see beginning tonight and Monday. I believe they were at least modestly impressed to take such action and assuming I’m right, this is just a tease en route to even more mature data covering at least 2 additional patients in January along with comments on newly added endpoints. This is just my opinion and not intended as investment advice.
